justification: A new read-only verification script, its unit tests, and a falsifiability proof driving the shared #890 harness. It reads production Supabase read-only and downloads published PDFs from R2. No writes, no migrations, no schema change, no served surface altered. Standard rather than minor because the script produces a PASS/FAIL judgement about the project's headline asset, and a wrong judgement here would either manufacture a crisis or conceal one. This commit adds the measure/write pair that corrected pdf_page on 8 rows (0.75% of the table): a read-only proposer, and a guarded writer that backs up, predicts to disk, guards each UPDATE on the expected pre-state and verifies afterwards. 8 applied, 0 skipped, row count 1071 unchanged, prediction matched 8/8. A second repair round corrected 11 more page citations (Waverley), resolved by the document's own chapter/section numbering after the value-only method left them ambiguous. 19 rows repaired in total; citation accuracy 85.3% -> 98.4%.

falsifiable_check.fails_when: Seven defects are planted into scripts/validate_controls_against_source_pdf.py one at a time and each must turn tests/test_controls_against_source_pdf.py red; the runner exits 1 if any survives, if the baseline is not already green, or if a plant fails to change the file sha256. Measured 7/7 CAUGHT, file restored byte-identically each time. The planted defects: (1) stop requiring the control number to be present, (2) stop requiring the subject wording to match, (3) soften DATA_MARK from 0.95 to 0.50, (4) treat could-not-check rows as checkable, (5) stop stripping clause markers, (6) stop preferring the stored value over numbers scraped from the quote, (7) stop folding ampersand into and. Separately, python -m pytest tests/test_controls_against_source_pdf.py -q must pass 35/35.
falsifiable_check.external_authority: The council's own published DCP PDF, fetched from R2. Nothing in this pipeline produced it, so it can disagree with us, which is the entire point. This is the first external authority the controls table has been compared against (ce-verified-capability-statement-2026-08 section 2.6d: not compared against anything).

pre_impl.existing_data: Four sweeps against origin/main f5acb080, recorded in the script prior-art-checked header. validate_control_source_values.py (#868) compares a value to its OWN stored quote and cannot fail when the quote came from the wrong place. validate_controls_provenance.py (#866) classifies provenance from the repo and never opens a document. link_controls_to_provisions.py (#867) matches against the ingested corpus, 42 of 1071 rows, and the corpus is itself extracted so it is not independent. measure_control_quote_gap.py measures why that match misses. numeric_control_review.py is nearest and its R2 download is REUSED, not copied. Frontend sweep: StateLevelControls, DcpStructuredControls, planning-controls route and api/dcp/structured-controls all render controls; none verifies one.
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: TWO assumptions were false and both were caught before any figure was reported. (1) source_text is documented everywhere as the verbatim sentence its number came from; for table-derived controls it is a reconstruction of a table cell plus its row and column labels, measured on marrickville id=534 where the PDF reads 'Seniors housing' and '0.2 per unit ... visitors & carers' under the heading 'Car spaces: Parking Area 1'. A contiguous-run test would have scored it near zero and reported a false crisis, so the method became value-presence plus term coverage. (2) pdf_page was assumed to locate the control; all 21 marrickville rows cite page 8 while the rate is on page 10, and the printed folio is the PDF index minus 4, so neither reading of the field matches. Data correctness and citation accuracy were therefore split into two separately reported measurements.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: New script. It is the third rung (validated against X) for an asset previously at rung 1-2 only, and it is deliberately additive: nothing existing changed behaviour. The .gitignore edit un-ignores the two new scripts, which sit under a blanket scripts/* exclusion with a per-file allow-list; without it both would have been silently untracked, the trap #866 already had to guard once.

functions.name: page_supports
functions.input: the control quote, one page's extracted text, and the control's stored value_min/value_max
functions.output: (supported, term_coverage, missing_values). Supported requires BOTH the stored value present on the page (accepted in metres or millimetres) AND at least 70% of the quote's distinguishing words. Two independent conditions: the value is the claim under test; the term coverage is what stops a bare number matching by coincidence on a 1563-page document.
functions.if_none: An empty page returns (False, 0.0, the required values). A row with no stored value and no numbers in its quote can never return True because bool(wanted) is part of the conjunction, so a vacuous pass is impossible.

functions.name: required_values
functions.input: value_min, value_max as stored (numeric or None)
functions.output: The numbers that must be found, each also offered in its millimetre/metre twin because a stored 0.9 is routinely published as 900mm.
functions.if_none: Returns empty rather than guessing. The caller then falls back to numbers scraped from the quote, and if there are none either, the row is classified no_numeric_value_to_check and excluded from the denominator.

functions.name: strip_clause_marker
functions.input: a control's stored source_text, which for DCP rows usually opens with a clause marker such as C.06 or O.01
functions.output: The same text with a leading clause marker (C.06, O.01, A.1.2) removed, so its digits are never read as a measurement.
functions.if_none: None or empty returns an empty string. A sentence that genuinely opens with a value (3 metres is the minimum...) is not matched by the marker pattern and keeps its number, pinned by test.

functions.name: classify
functions.input: one control row plus the full page-text map of its cited document
functions.output: Exactly one of eight verdicts: supported_on_cited_page, supported_on_another_page (carrying the real page and the offset), unsupported_by_document, cited_page_past_end_of_document, document_has_no_text_layer, document_unavailable, row_has_no_source_text, no_numeric_value_to_check.
functions.if_none: Every not-checkable condition has its OWN verdict rather than collapsing into a failure or a pass, and all four are excluded from the denominator, which is printed beside every rate.

values.value: dcp_setback_controls.value_min / value_max — the control's stored number, and the thing under test. Column names read from information_schema, not inferred.
values.read_at: scripts/validate_controls_against_source_pdf.py ROWS_SQL, consumed by required_values() and compared against the PDF page text.
values.if_missing: 14 of the 152 rows store neither. The row is classified no_numeric_value_to_check and excluded from the denominator — never a pass, never a failure. These are legitimate: Waverley and Woollahra front setbacks are character-based and the DCP sets no numeric minimum.

values.value: dcp_setback_controls.pdf_page — the page the row claims its value came from. 193 of 1071 rows carry one; 152 are current and join to a fetchable document.
values.read_at: Same query; consumed by classify() to build the ±1 page window.
values.if_missing: 919 controls have no page and are outside this check entirely. Reported as a coverage limit (14%), never silently treated as covered.

values.value: dcp_setback_controls.source_text — the quote, used only for its distinguishing words, not as a verbatim string.
values.read_at: Same query; consumed by distinctive_terms() after strip_clause_marker().
values.if_missing: Verdict row_has_no_source_text, inside COULD_NOT_CHECK, excluded from the denominator.

values.value: dcp_chapter_registry.r2_current_path — the object key of the council's published PDF.
values.read_at: Same query, joined on (council = lga, chapter_key = source_chapter_key); consumed by download_from_r2().
values.if_missing: Rows without a path are excluded by the WHERE clause. A path that fails to download yields document_unavailable, printed per document, never a pass.

queries.purpose: Select every current control that cites a page and joins to a fetchable published document — the checkable population.
queries.file_line: scripts/validate_controls_against_source_pdf.py ROWS_SQL (module constant, executed once in main())
queries.where_clause: c.pdf_page IS NOT NULL AND c.is_current = TRUE AND g.r2_current_path IS NOT NULL AND g.r2_current_path <> '' — scoped to current rows so superseded controls are not judged, and to rows with a document so an unreachable PDF cannot masquerade as a failure. Runs under SET statement_timeout = '60s' on a connection pinned conn.set_session(readonly=True). No writes, no DDL.

break_it.scenario: A clause marker's digits are counted as a control value.
break_it.what_happens: C.06 On corner lots ... minimum of 3 metres yields numbers 6 and 3, which then match a page discussing 600m2 suburban lots, and the row passes on the wrong page.
break_it.how: strip_clause_marker removes the marker before any number is read, and the stored value_min/value_max takes precedence over quote-scraped numbers. Three tests pin it; planting its removal turns the suite red.
break_it.repro: Not hypothetical: measured live on parramatta id=563 and it produced the first run's inflated 99.3%.

break_it.scenario: A control that legitimately has no number is reported as unsupported.
break_it.what_happens: Waverley and Woollahra character-based front setbacks (consistent with the predominant setback of adjacent development) have no numeric minimum by design. Thirteen correct rows were failed, manufacturing a defect out of good data.
break_it.how: no_numeric_value_to_check is its own verdict inside COULD_NOT_CHECK, excluded from the denominator and never counted as a pass.
break_it.repro: Measured: 14 of the 152 rows store no value; the run reported 84.9% before this was separated and 91.5% after.

break_it.scenario: A bare number matches by coincidence on a very long document.
break_it.what_happens: Parramatta's DCP is 1563 pages, so almost any small number appears somewhere and a value-only test would pass nearly everything.
break_it.how: 70% term coverage is required on the same page as the value. Planting the removal of the coverage condition turns the suite red.

break_it.scenario: A PDF is a scanned image with no text layer.
break_it.what_happens: Every control in it reads as unsupported, producing a false mass failure.
break_it.how: document_has_no_text_layer is a distinct verdict inside COULD_NOT_CHECK. Observed live: 3 of 23 marrickville pages and 1 of 48 georges_river pages carry no text.

break_it.scenario: R2 credentials are absent or a fetch fails.
break_it.what_happens: The run silently checks nothing and reports a clean pass.
break_it.how: document_unavailable is a distinct verdict, the failure is printed per document, and a run where nothing is checkable returns 'nothing could be checked -- that is not a pass' and exits 1.

break_it.scenario: The pass mark is softened after seeing a disappointing result.
break_it.what_happens: The check becomes a formality, exactly the DQ-30 0%-drift failure in a new costume.
break_it.how: DATA_MARK is a module constant documented as fixed before the first fetch, pinned by a test, and planting a change to it turns the suite red. Citation accuracy is reported UNGRADED precisely because one case was inspected during pre-implementation.
break_it.repro: python scripts/prove_controls_pdf_check.py, case 'soften the pass mark to 50%'

break_it.scenario: A missing library silently skips the check.
break_it.what_happens: A green run that verified nothing, the pattern that left 23 tests dark for months.
break_it.how: fitz and psycopg2 are imported at module scope with no try/except and no importorskip, so an absent library is an immediate RED. numeric_control_review.py's try/except-to-None is called out in the header as the anti-pattern.
break_it.repro: Rename the fitz package and run the script; it raises ImportError rather than reporting a pass.

break_it.scenario: A --limit debug run is read as a full gate result.
break_it.what_happens: The rate describes only the documents the caller chose to fetch, but the script printed PASS and exited 0, so a partial run is indistinguishable from a complete one.
break_it.how: A --limit run that actually skipped documents prints INCONCLUSIVE with the skipped count and returns 2. A partial run can never exit 0.

break_it.scenario: A wrong page reference is replaced by a guessed one, so it looks repaired and nobody re-checks it.
break_it.what_happens: The 11 ambiguous Waverley rows each have several pages carrying the value in a 448-page document; picking the first would write a differently-wrong page that now carries an air of verification.
break_it.how: A correction is proposed ONLY where exactly one page in the whole document carries the value at >=80% term coverage. Ambiguous (11) and not-in-document (12) are reported and never written.
break_it.repro: python scripts/measure_control_page_corrections.py — states: already_correct 110, single_candidate 8, ambiguous 11, not_in_document 12, not_testable 11.

break_it.scenario: A row changed between measurement and write, and the write clobbers the newer value.
break_it.what_happens: Another session's repair is silently overwritten with a stale proposal.
break_it.how: Every UPDATE carries WHERE id = %s AND pdf_page = %s (the expected pre-state); a non-matching row yields rowcount 0, is counted as SKIPPED and printed. Pre-state of all 8 rows is backed up before the first write and the predicted after-state is written to disk before any row changes.

break_it.scenario: A page correction is derived in a scratchpad script that is never committed.
break_it.what_happens: The 11 Waverley repairs become unreproducible hand-work — the exact failure the extraction post-mortem names, and the reason half the controls table has no recipe.
break_it.how: scripts/resolve_control_page_by_clause.py is committed and allow-listed past the blanket scripts/* ignore; re-running it regenerates the same 11 (council, clause, page) triples.

mutation_analysis: Seven mutations planted through the shared #890 harness, all seven caught, each restored byte-identically and verified by sha256 in a finally block. The two that matter most reproduce real incidents rather than hypotheticals: stop-stripping-clause-markers reproduces the measured parramatta id=563 false positive and the zone-probe trap where Woollahra C1 (Control 1) and Ashfield E1 (a chapter label) were counted as zone codes; count-could-not-check-as-checkable reproduces the denominator inflation that would let unfetchable documents read as passes. On strength rather than volume: the 35 unit tests cover a pure core with no I/O, so a mutation cannot be masked by a network or database dependency.
residual_risk: THE HEADLINE NUMBER IS NOT A LIST OF CONFIRMED ERRORS. Twelve controls are reported unsupported; none has been confirmed by a human opening the PDF. At least one (wingecarribee id=1160) missed on term coverage by three percentage points, which is a threshold artifact rather than a data defect, so the true error count is at most 12 and possibly well below. The 70% coverage threshold and the plus-or-minus-1 page tolerance are judgement calls with no external basis. Coverage is 14% of the table: 919 controls record no page and are untouched, so nothing here licenses a claim about the other 86%. Citation accuracy (85.3%) is measured but ungraded this run and must not be quoted as a passed test. Finally, this checks that a number APPEARS on a page alongside matching words; it does not read the sentence, so a control could be supported by text that means the opposite, and only a human reading can settle that.

post_merge.db_reset: A production write WAS performed: pdf_page corrected on 8 of 1071 dcp_setback_controls rows. Backup data/db_rollback_backups/control_pdf_pages_pre_repair_2026-08-09.json; rollback is UPDATE dcp_setback_controls SET pdf_page=<pdf_page> WHERE id=<id> from that file. Verified: 8 applied, 0 skipped, row count 1071 before and after, prediction matched 8/8, and an independent re-run of the checker moved citation accuracy 85.3% -> 91.5%. SECOND WRITE: pdf_page corrected on 11 further rows (Waverley), backup data/db_rollback_backups/control_pdf_pages_pre_repair_2026-08-09-waverley.json, 11 applied, 0 skipped, 1071/989 rows unchanged, prediction matched 11/11, citation accuracy verified 91.5% -> 98.4% by re-run.
post_merge.secrets: No. Credentials are read from the bare repo .env into os.environ and never printed; the R2 client is constructed from them and no key, token or connection string is logged. PDFs are cached to the OS temp directory, not the repo.
post_merge.manual_verify: Open the twelve unsupported controls' PDFs at the cited page and read them, to separate real extraction errors from threshold artifacts. Then decide whether the 919 controls with no pdf_page should have one backfilled, since without it they cannot be checked by this method at all.
